key_insight: By tracing a beta hairpin and using counterfactual interventions on latents, the paper shows ESMFold implements folding in two computational stages: early blocks inject pairwise biochemical signals (residue identity, charge flow) from sequence representations, and later blocks convert those signals into 3D geometry.
problem_solved: Explains how a large protein structure model internally performs folding—providing causal, layer-wise mechanistic attribution rather than black‑box predictions.
method: Trace folding dynamics of a beta hairpin through ESMFold’s blocks and representations (sequence latents → pairwise latents → structure).
Apply counterfactual interventions on latent features to test causal roles (e.g., swap/ablate residue or charge signals) and observe structural consequences.
Layer-wise analysis to identify two computational stages: initialization of biochemical pairwise signals in early blocks and geometric refinement in later blocks.
impact: Gives practitioners causal, actionable insight into where and how biochemical information is encoded in folding models—enabling targeted debugging, architecture improvements, and principled interventions for design and efficiency.
visual_elements: Two-stage flow diagram: (1) early blocks: sequence → pairwise biochemical signals (residue identity, charge flow), (2) later blocks: pairwise → 3D coordinates.
Schematic of counterfactual latent intervention showing before/after structure when specific latent signals are altered.
Layer-wise heatmap/timeline showing emergence and propagation of pairwise biochemical signals across model blocks.
Overlay of predicted beta hairpin vs. counterfactual-altered predictions to illustrate causal effect on fold.
paper_title: Mechanisms of AI Protein Folding in ESMFold
paper_authors: Kevin Lu, Jannik Brinkmann, Stefan Huber, Aaron Mueller, Yonatan Belinkov
